authored_assumptions: All geometry, hidden surfaces, mechanical details and material finishes are authored locally; no image-to-3D recovery or external assets are used.
The original blue/cream robot identity, all 17 bone names, parent relationships, major pivots, left-hand board and right-hand probe are retained.
Anatomical left is world +X, right is world -X, the rest-facing direction is -Y and units are meters with Z up before glTF export.
Closed body lofts and beveled panels are overlapping manufactured components, not one welded watertight outer surface.
The visible grip fingers and thumb are rigidly weighted to each hand bone; they are not independent finger joints or finger controls.
Board traces, pads and chip pins are static decorative geometry; probe motion and inspection are authored gestures, not contact-constrained manufacturing or a circuit simulation.
The four clips have matching authored endpoints as loop intent only. Rendered loop boundaries and state quality require downstream verification.
This general-profile revision uses real metallic-roughness PBR and richer geometry. It is not the matte diffuse weft-v1 deliverable and has not been validated against Weft.
Original bone rests are retained, while new shell surfaces, backside panels and small surface patterns are deliberate design assumptions.
Keyframe rotations and translations use model-rest axes; the backend converts them through bone rest bases.

HD textures are seeded, locally authored procedural patterns at native1024/2048 resolution, not neural output, reference-extracted texture maps or evidence of photorealism. Studio floor and exposure are render settings, not simulation geometry.

authoring.method: Deterministic local Python geometry and keyframe authoring; no generation service calls
authoring.status: Authored scene; rendering, exported mesh validation and visual review are downstream work

hd_upgrade.edit_prompt: Preserve this character/object's exact base mesh components, proportions, palettes, accessories, bone rests and four skeletal actions. Add native-resolution 1024/2048 procedural basecolor and tangent-normal textures with irregular fine surface detail, not an enlarged 512px bitmap. Use a grounded soft studio with world strength0.3 and exposure0.55. Do not claim exact Muse reconstruction or equal visual quality before rendering and comparison. Keep all sources and all prior recipes unchanged. Use two bounded HD brushed-metal finishes only; retain enamel, rubber, glass-like and paper material identities. Do not add animal fur.
hd_upgrade.exact_user_request: you're working on making these avatars better right? I want the same textures and hd quality as the muse ones for example fura and hari
hd_upgrade.prior_source_prompt: Create a genuinely new complete humanoid robot, not a lamp or an animal reskin. Give it a rounded blue torso, cream front panel, friendly dark visor with two warm eyes, small antenna, two articulated arms and legs with real elbow/knee pivots, solid toy hands and broad feet. Anatomical left is world +X and right is world -X for a front facing -Y. Use only opaque matte diffuse materials with metallic=0 and roughness=1 exactly. The left hand carries a small circuit workpiece and the right holds an assembly probe. Idle gently rocks; making_something uses short probe strokes at the low-held workpiece; working raises the workpiece for inspection; milestone_level_up raises both tools with one joyful hop. Key only the ten body-frame bones; head/hands/feet/tool descendants keep authored local rest transforms. Supply editable scene data, real skin weights and complete hidden surfaces for weft-v1; do not change or simulate Weft physics, actions or rewards.

glb.skeletal_clips: All four original clips preserved unchanged

hd_upgrade.source_prompt:
Refine the existing blue-and-cream workshop robot into a coherent,
polished character model, preserving its dark friendly visor, warm eyes, compact
antenna, anatomical left-hand circuit board and right-hand assembly probe. Replace
the inflated primitive appearance with deliberately shaped, closed shell geometry:
a tapered rounded-rectangle blue body, inset ivory chest armor, layered panel gaps,
recessed controls, a two-piece head enclosure and a dark visor in a substantial
gasket. Keep the face warm and legible, with softly rounded eyes and a curved smile.
Use chamfered enamel shells, satin ivory panels, dark joint seals and selectively
brushed aluminum/brass hardware, all as native opaque glTF metallic-roughness PBR.
Construct shoulder, elbow, hip, knee and wrist collars around the real pivots.
Give the hands a palm, three visible static grip fingers and a thumb; these are
authored rigid details, not newly actuated finger joints. Model a purposeful rear
service hatch, recessed vent bars, fasteners, heel guards and rubber soles so the
back and sides are complete, not implied by the portrait. Detail the circuit board
with a raised chip, fixed copper traces, pads, pins and edge hardware; make the
probe a layered grip, collar, shaft and tapered tip. Preserve all 17 named bones,
four meaningful states and rigid skin weights. Idle gently settles, working lifts
the board for inspection, making_something makes short probe gestures near its
fixed guide, and milestone_level_up raises the hands into an open V with a small
hop. Limit the celebration forearm rotations to 1.10 radians so the tools stay
outside the head silhouette. Keep hidden geometry, mechanics, material finishes
and gestures explicitly authored; do not claim reconstructed reference geometry,
physical manufacture, finger actuation, seamless loops or Weft compatibility for
this richer general-profile model. Use no external models, textures or fonts.

studio_grounding.method: Conservative authored rest bounds of named contact parts, including configured maximum fur length; not simulated ground contact

states.meaning: An attentive settling sway with a small head tilt, tools held steadily at waist level.
Lifts the circuit board below the visor and studies it with a gentle head-and-body scan; the probe rests low.
Makes short precise probe gestures near the board's contact guide while the left hand steadies it. Copper tracks are fixed geometry, not newly manufactured marks.
Raises both tools into a wide open V with a small hop and preparatory knee bend; hands stay outside the face silhouette.
